key_insight: In the Bern Sleep-Wake Registry, gpt-oss-20b extracted comorbidities with an F1 of 0.88 and matched the earliest reported diagnosis date to the exact day in 86.73% of cases.
clinical_relevance: Automated extraction of diagnoses and reported dates could support longitudinal registry research while reducing direct annotation costs.
method: Analyzed 2,343 clinical entries from 248 patients across 32 diagnostic categories in six comorbidity groups.
Used gpt-oss-20b to extract diagnosis presence, instance counts, and associated dates.
Compared outputs with independent annotations by two physicians, adjudicated by a third.
evidence_signal: Against the adjudicated reference, cumulative-date recall was 87.63%, full date-set agreement was 58.19%, and direct annotation costs were reduced by 94.65%.
watch_item: A 20.88% extra-date rate and substantial human temporal disagreement highlight the need for careful date validation; reported dates should not be assumed to represent disease onset.
paper_title: Bern Sleep-Wake Registry: temporal extraction of comorbidities from unstructured clinical text using a large language model
